A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
attention is a cholinergic function, but the cholinergic system does not seem to be the only system responsible for attention.
the cholinergic hypothesis of cognitive impairment in schizophrenia is not supported.
the cholinergic system in the prefrontal cortex plays an important role in sustained attention, but that the cholinesterases and benzodiazepines may not have a direct role in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cholinergic modulation of attentional performance is not a simple process and that the effects of drugs on attentional processes are likely to be complex.
the effects of cholinergic manipulations on attention are complex and that the effects of such manipulations on attention may be dependent upon the extent of cortical cholinergenic deafferentation.

the cholinergic deafferenation model of sustained attention deficits is robust and not likely to be overcome by pharmacological interventions that do not specifically augment cortical acetylcholine levels.
